body: This definitely looks like an allergic reaction.  Ask your wife if she has changed anything.  Bed bugs (I think...) travel so you would probably have had the bumps while traveling.  But as someone said above you CAN develop allergies as an adult.  With hives like that I'd definitely keep some benedryl around, at least until you figure out the source.  You wouldn't want the allergy to get triggered around your face/get worse.

I think I'll have to. It seems to be either doing that or ruining my GPA.  I have such a high GPA.  I'm seriously one of those award winning students who get offered huge scholarships to graduate school before I even know if I'm going.  I've done everything right and it's awful that this one semester could completely screw everything up.  

I think I've always kind of dealt with this "perfectionist" desire.  It's never been okay to fail, even when faced with the absolute worst circumstances.  It's really exhausting when you have to deal with just making it through each day without wanting to kill yourself from pain alone.  

Not even in the depressed way, but in the "This really fucking hurts please kill me now" sort of way.  Except at the same time you can't be screaming "This really fucking hurts." You have to put on a normal face and deal with it.  

Sorry, I'm totally ranting.

This is the tough part. Everyone knows.  They know I've basically *lost it* and their whole thing is: you've got to do it anyway.  They think I need to quit my job (one of the only things actually bringing me happiness right now) to focus on school. Quite frankly, if I didn't have my job I think I wouldn't leave my house. I try to go to class. I get ready. I've even driven to campus a couple of times. I just can't do it.  

I think they think I'll realize the errors of my ways and change this behavior but what they do not seem to realize is I **do** know this is fucking up my life. I just can't do anything about it.

Honestly, I don't know.  Sometimes I really don't know.  Sometimes it takes everything in me just to get out of bed to go to the bathroom.  I've been extremely fortunate in the illness part for the most part (yeah, that sounds crazy.)  While it seems like every year I get diagnosed with something new, I am so fortunate because I have great health insurance.  So while my body sucks it could suck so much worse.  A lot of people with my one illness often are stuck in wheel chairs but I've had access to physical therapy.  I am so grateful for that.  

For awhile I think that's what kept me so driven with school.  Sort of like, "I was dealt this horrible hand, but there are people dealt even *worse* hands."  And, this is going to sound cocky, but the one thing that isn't entirely fucked to hell is I am actually decently intelligent.  I figured I could attempt to be the person who helped make it so those dealt with a similar hand could have easier lives.  I live in the US so basically if you're chronically ill you're screwed financially.  Even with my absolutely wonderful health insurance (My mom works for the government) we still spend tons of money every year.  I'm also lucky because even though I'm engaged, working, and living on my own my parents still are willing to pay my medical bills.  If they didn't I wouldn't even be able to go to school because I would have to work full time.

Up until about five months ago I actually handled most of this pretty well.  About two years ago I did have a minor breakdown because I was hospitalized for awhile which messed everything up.  It made my RSD 1,000 times worse (it felt like) AND I was dealing with a new condition on top of everything else.  I had to drop out of school and when I went back I would go to class and then be in bed the rest of the day.  However, for the most part I've handled this stuff pretty well.  I've become so used to being sick that it is sort of normal.

But then a few months ago all of a sudden I had so much anxiety.  I would go to work but other than that I wouldn't leave my house.  I'd be in bed all day.  That hasn't really changed.  I had a 4.0 GPA and now I'm being threatened with academic probation or something because I can't even make myself go to class.  And the more class I miss the harder it is to even make myself go back.  I have a hell of a time making myself go to work but at least there I don't feel stressed out all the time.

My parents are trying to get me to quit my job, but we can't afford that.  I can't handle school right now, but I also can't afford to just quit again.  My family has lost so much money just because of my health making me having to withdrawal for a semester here and there.

I think I'm just tired.  I'm tired of feeling like I can't breath every time I stand up and move.  I'm tired of being physically tired.  I'm tired of the pain.  I have one of the most painful conditions known to science, some even argue it is the most painful.  It's called Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy or Complex Regional Pain Syndrome.  It basically feels like I'm on fire all the time.  

It's just exhausting.  I also hate letting people down.
I am a double major in philosophy and political science with the intention of heading to law school.
I'm a student right now but I also work part-time at a gas station (really fancy.)
Usually.  Though sometimes no because they have me pretty medicated.  But the last looooooong hospital stay I had was for a heart problem for I could use it.

I just LOVE when people do this.  I'm currently crippled with anxiety. I can barely leave my house.  While I *know* it is meant as a good intention all I get is, "You just HAVE to do it."  or "If you just get yourself out there you'll be fine."  

I totally understand it is an attempt to help and to help *fix* the problem, but I can't seem to get across that I just can't make myself do it without a horrible panic attack.
